section: Revolt of 1857 - economic, socio-religious, administrative and military causes
subsections: Immediate cause - Enfield rifle, greased cartridges, rumours, chapatis
Military grievances - GSEA, bhatta, discrimination, troop ratio
Contemporary Indian writings on the causes - author and book

accepted.s: The Pattern 1853 Enfield rifle was introduced into the army in:
accepted.x: The new Pattern 1853 Enfield rifle was introduced into the army in December 1856.
accepted.tq: Use the precise date rather than the better-known date of the uprising.
accepted.sec: Immediate cause - Enfield rifle, greased cartridges, rumours, chapatis

accepted.s: Why did the cartridges of the new Enfield rifle offend both Hindu and Muslim sepoys?
o: They were believed to contain cow and pig fat, and had to be bitten open.
They required sepoys to cross the sea before use.
They were made exclusively from animal skin.
They were distributed only to European soldiers.
accepted.x: The greased-paper cartridges were believed to contain cow fat, offensive to Hindus, and pig fat, offensive to Muslims. Sepoys had to bite them open before loading.
accepted.tq: Identify the religious implication of the practical loading procedure.
accepted.sec: Immediate cause - Enfield rifle, greased cartridges, rumours, chapatis

accepted.s: The cartridge controversy was interpreted by many sepoys as evidence of:
o: A policy to promote Indian officers above Subedars
A colonial-missionary plot to defile religion and force conversion
A plan to reduce the size of the Bengal Army
accepted.x: The cartridges were viewed as final proof of a colonial-missionary conspiracy to defile Indian religions and compel conversion.
accepted.tq: Test the interpretation attached to an immediate cause.
accepted.sec: Immediate cause - Enfield rifle, greased cartridges, rumours, chapatis

accepted.s: Which one of the following rumours circulated before the Revolt of 1857?
o: Cow blood was being mixed in government wells only.
Bone dust was being mixed in Company flour.
Gunpowder was being mixed with salt in army stores.
Cholera germs were being mixed in postal letters.
accepted.x: A rumour spread that bone dust was being mixed in the flour supplied by the East India Company.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the specific rumour from unrelated allegations.
accepted.sec: Immediate cause - Enfield rifle, greased cartridges, rumours, chapatis

accepted.s: The mysterious chapatis associated with the events preceding the Revolt of 1857 were passed from village to village across:
accepted.x: Mysterious chapatis were passed from village to village across North India in early 1857.
accepted.tq: Test the geographical association of a distinctive event.
accepted.sec: Immediate cause - Enfield rifle, greased cartridges, rumours, chapatis

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the early refusals and outbreaks connected with the Revolt of 1857:
1. The 19th Native Infantry refused at Berhampur in February 1857.
2. Mangal Pandey's action occurred at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857.
3. The Meerut rising began on 10 May 1857.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the 19th Native Infantry acted at Berhampur in February, Mangal Pandey acted at Barrackpore on 29 March, and the Meerut rising began on 10 May 1857.
accepted.tq: Link the three events through their locations and dates.
accepted.sec: Immediate cause - Enfield rifle, greased cartridges, rumours, chapatis

accepted.s: Mangal Pandey, associated with the Barrackpore incident, belonged to the:
accepted.x: Mangal Pandey was a sepoy of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry.
accepted.tq: Use the person-regiment association to separate closely related incidents.
accepted.sec: Immediate cause - Enfield rifle, greased cartridges, rumours, chapatis

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Barrackpore episode involving Mangal Pandey?
o: He attacked General Canning and was executed on 10 May 1857.
He led the 85 cavalrymen at Meerut and was executed on 9 May 1857.
He attacked Lieutenant Baugh and Sergeant-Major Hewson and was executed on 8 April 1857.
He refused service at Berhampur and was executed in February 1857.
accepted.x: Mangal Pandey attacked Lieutenant Baugh and Sergeant-Major Hewson at Barrackpore and was executed on 8 April 1857.
accepted.tq: Match the correct person with the deed and date.
accepted.sec: Immediate cause - Enfield rifle, greased cartridges, rumours, chapatis

accepted.s: What was the immediate administrative consequence for Mangal Pandey's regiment after the Barrackpore episode?
o: It was merged with the European regiments.
It was placed under the command of Mangal Pandey.
accepted.x: The 34th Bengal Native Infantry, Mangal Pandey's regiment, was disbanded after the incident.
accepted.tq: Test the institutional consequence rather than the event itself.
accepted.sec: Immediate cause - Enfield rifle, greased cartridges, rumours, chapatis

accepted.s: At Meerut, the 85 sepoys of the 3rd Cavalry were court-martialled on 9 May 1857 and sentenced to:
accepted.x: The 85 sepoys of the 3rd Cavalry were court-martialled on 9 May 1857 and given ten years' imprisonment, helping precipitate the rising on 10 May.
accepted.tq: Separate the punishment date from the date of the uprising.
accepted.sec: Immediate cause - Enfield rifle, greased cartridges, rumours, chapatis

accepted.s: The General Service Enlistment Act of 1856 was associated with the administration of:
accepted.x: The General Service Enlistment Act was enacted under Lord Canning in 1856.
accepted.tq: Apply the ruler-or-authority association trap.
accepted.sec: Military grievances - GSEA, bhatta, discrimination, troop ratio

accepted.s: The General Service Enlistment Act, 1856 required new recruits to:
o: Serve only within their home province
Receive equal pay with European soldiers
accepted.x: The Act required new recruits to serve anywhere, including overseas. Orthodox Hindus feared that sea travel would cause loss of caste.
accepted.tq: Infer the military grievance from the service obligation.
accepted.sec: Military grievances - GSEA, bhatta, discrimination, troop ratio

accepted.s: Why did overseas service create anxiety among orthodox Hindu sepoys?
o: Crossing the sea was believed to cause loss of caste.
It suspended their promotion to Subedar.
It involved compulsory conversion to Christianity.
It made them ineligible for bhatta in Punjab.
accepted.x: Orthodox Hindus believed that crossing the sea resulted in loss of caste, making the overseas-service requirement deeply unpopular.
accepted.tq: Connect a military rule with its socio-religious consequence.
accepted.sec: Military grievances - GSEA, bhatta, discrimination, troop ratio

accepted.s: Bhatta, whose withdrawal angered the sepoys, was a:
accepted.x: Bhatta was the foreign service allowance paid to soldiers serving outside their ordinary area.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between military pay components with similar administrative associations.
accepted.sec: Military grievances - GSEA, bhatta, discrimination, troop ratio

accepted.s: Bhatta was withdrawn for service in:
accepted.x: Bhatta was withdrawn for service in Sindh and Punjab after these areas became British territory.
accepted.tq: Pair the allowance grievance with the correct territories.
accepted.sec: Military grievances - GSEA, bhatta, discrimination, troop ratio

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a military grievance of the Indian sepoys mentioned in relation to the Revolt of 1857?
o: The ceiling of promotion at the rank of Subedar
accepted.x: Inefficiency of officers was identified as not being a cause of sepoy anger. Lower pay, racial contempt and the Subedar ceiling were genuine grievances.
accepted.tq: Find the one item expressly excluded from the list of grievances.
accepted.sec: Military grievances - GSEA, bhatta, discrimination, troop ratio

accepted.s: An Indian sepoy in the pre-1857 army could ordinarily rise no higher than:
accepted.x: Racial discrimination restricted the highest rank ordinarily attainable by an Indian soldier to Subedar.
accepted.tq: Test the exact promotion ceiling rather than general discrimination.
accepted.sec: Military grievances - GSEA, bhatta, discrimination, troop ratio

accepted.s: Which Act ended free postage for sepoys?
accepted.x: Free postage for sepoys was ended by the Post Office Act of 1854.
accepted.tq: Match a specific grievance with the legislation that caused it.
accepted.sec: Military grievances - GSEA, bhatta, discrimination, troop ratio

accepted.s: On the eve of the Revolt of 1857, the approximate ratio of Indian sepoys to European soldiers in India was:
accepted.x: There were about 2.3 lakh Indian sepoys and 45,000 European soldiers, giving an approximate ratio of 5:1.
accepted.tq: Convert the supplied troop figures into the approximate ratio.
accepted.sec: Military grievances - GSEA, bhatta, discrimination, troop ratio

accepted.s: Which pair correctly represents the approximate military strength on the eve of the Revolt of 1857?
o: 3 lakh Indian sepoys and 1 lakh Europeans
accepted.x: The Indian army consisted of approximately 2.3 lakh sepoys compared with about 45,000 European soldiers.
accepted.tq: Read both sides of a numerical comparison instead of relying only on the ratio.
accepted.sec: Military grievances - GSEA, bhatta, discrimination, troop ratio

accepted.s: The European troops in India had been reduced in part because they had been drawn off for the:
accepted.x: European troops had been drawn away for the Crimean and Persian wars, contributing to the imbalance in troop strength.
accepted.tq: Identify the two wars connected with the troop shortage.
accepted.sec: Military grievances - GSEA, bhatta, discrimination, troop ratio

accepted.s: Awadh was called the “nursery of the Bengal Army” because:
o: It was the only province where European soldiers were recruited.
Many Bengal Army sepoys were high-caste men from Awadh and carried regional grievances into the army.
It housed the headquarters of the Bengal Army exclusively.
It was the birthplace of the Enfield rifle.
accepted.x: The Bengal Army recruited many high-caste men from Awadh. Its annexation in 1856 therefore angered a large section of the sepoys.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional metaphor to infer its concrete meaning.
accepted.sec: Military grievances - GSEA, bhatta, discrimination, troop ratio

accepted.s: The expression “peasants in uniform” referred to the fact that the sepoys:
o: Were recruited only from European farming communities
Were trained exclusively in agricultural work
Received land grants instead of salaries
Carried rural and village grievances into the army
accepted.x: The sepoys were largely drawn from rural communities, so their grievances reflected those of the villages from which they came.
accepted.tq: Translate a descriptive phrase into its historical implication.
accepted.sec: Military grievances - GSEA, bhatta, discrimination, troop ratio

accepted.s: Who wrote *Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind* on the causes of the Indian Revolt?
accepted.x: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan wrote *Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind*, meaning “The Causes of the Indian Revolt.”
accepted.tq: Match the author with the exact title of the work.
accepted.sec: Contemporary Indian writings on the causes - author and book

accepted.s: *Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind* was written in:
accepted.x: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan's work was written in Urdu during 1858–59.
accepted.tq: Test the language of a named historical source.
accepted.sec: Contemporary Indian writings on the causes - author and book

accepted.s: Vishnubhat Godse is associated with which of the following works?
o: *The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857*
accepted.x: Vishnubhat Godse wrote *Majha Pravas*, a Marathi eyewitness travelogue.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure author–work pair in a literary match.
accepted.sec: Contemporary Indian writings on the causes - author and book

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: V.D. Savarkar — *The Indian War of Independence*
accepted.x: V.D. Savarkar wrote *The Indian War of Independence*. *Majha Pravas* was written by Vishnubhat Godse, *Rebellion 1857: A Symposium* by P.C. Joshi, and *Eighteen Fifty-Seven* by S.N. Sen.
accepted.tq: Use author–work matching to reject swapped literary attributions.
accepted.sec: Contemporary Indian writings on the causes - author and book

accepted.s: V.D. Savarkar's *The Indian War of Independence* was published in:
accepted.x: V.D. Savarkar's work *The Indian War of Independence* was published in 1909.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the publication year from the revolt and later historical works.
accepted.sec: Contemporary Indian writings on the causes - author and book

accepted.s:
Arrange the following works in chronological order of publication:
A. *Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind*
B. *The Indian War of Independence*
C. *Eighteen Fifty-Seven*
D. *Majha Pravas*
accepted.x: *Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind* appeared in 1858–59, followed by *Majha Pravas*, then Savarkar's work in 1909, and S.N. Sen's *Eighteen Fifty-Seven* in 1957.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest works first, then place the middle entries.
accepted.sec: Contemporary Indian writings on the causes - author and book

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with its author?
o: *Religion and Ideology of the Rebels of 1857* — S.N. Sen
accepted.x: P.C. Joshi wrote *Rebellion 1857: A Symposium*. G.B. Malleson wrote *The Indian Mutiny of 1857*, Christopher Hibbert wrote *The Great Mutiny*, and Iqbal Hussain wrote *Religion and Ideology of the Rebels of 1857*.
accepted.tq: Reject swapped authors by checking the exact author–title combination.
accepted.sec: Contemporary Indian writings on the causes - author and book

accepted.s: Who wrote *The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857*?
accepted.x: R.C. Majumdar wrote *The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857*.
accepted.tq: Test a single author–title association from a cluster of historical writings.
accepted.sec: Contemporary Indian writings on the causes - author and book

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Iqbal Hussain — *Religion and Ideology of the Rebels of 1857*
Khan Mohammad Sadiq Khan — *Excavation of Truth*
P.E. Roberts — *The Causes of the Indian Revolt*
accepted.x: P.E. Roberts was associated with the description of the revolt as “just a sepoy mutiny,” not with a work titled *The Causes of the Indian Revolt*. *Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind*, meaning “The Causes of the Indian Revolt,” was written by Sir Syed Ahmed Khan.
accepted.tq: Detect the familiar title wrongly assigned to a different author.
accepted.sec: Contemporary Indian writings on the causes - author and book

accepted.s: P.E. Roberts described the Revolt of 1857 as:
o: A religious war against the British
The First War of Indian Independence
accepted.x: P.E. Roberts characterized the revolt as “just a sepoy mutiny,” particularly in connection with the cartridge issue.
accepted.tq: Separate the British interpretive label from the nationalist interpretation.
accepted.sec: Contemporary Indian writings on the causes - author and book

accepted.s:
According to Sir Syed Ahmed Khan, which of the following contributed to the outbreak of the Revolt of 1857?
1. Lack of Indian representation in the Legislative Council
2. Misunderstanding of Indian customs
3. Complete equality between Indian and British soldiers
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan blamed the lack of Indian representation in the Legislative Council and the misunderstanding of Indian customs. Complete equality between Indian and British soldiers was not a cause identified by him.
accepted.tq: Use the contradiction in the third statement to isolate the two supported causes.
accepted.sec: Contemporary Indian writings on the causes - author and book
